prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts an outdoor street corridor where the ground plane brightens near the bottom and darkens into the central distance, flanked by a bright vendor cart on the left (1.5–2.5 m away) and multi-story buildings on the right (8–15 m away). In Frame 1, a yellow flatbed truck on the lower right is roughly 2–4 m from the camera wearer before retreating down the street to about 8–20 m across Frames 2–5, while a pedestrian in white pants and a blue shirt approaches along the middle of the road from roughly 8 m in Frame 1 to 2 m on the right in Frame 5, and a scooter rider approaches on the right in Frame 4 (~4–5 m) before exiting right. In Frames 4 and 5, a black helmet appears in the lower-left foreground within arm's reach (<0.5 m) of the camera wearer, partially occluding the lower edge of the vendor cart, while two standing pedestrians near the right building (~7–9 m away in Frames 1–3) and two seated people behind the left stall (Frames 4–5, ~2.5–3.5 m away) remain separated by several metres from the walking pedestrian. The depth map clarifies the continuous distance gradient along the road and immediately isolates the near-field helmet and cart awning overhead relative to the receding truck, which is harder to gauge quantitatively from RGB perspective alone. However, it is unreliable on fine structures—filling in the gaps between the truck's side-rail bars in Frame 1, blurring the parked scooters behind the cart into a single mass, and rendering the sky and distant trees past 25 m uniformly black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and mid-ground objects against a black background, tracking the approaching central pedestrian (from ~8 m in Frame 1 to ~2 m on the right in Frame 5) as he walks forward facing the camera wearer while holding a phone within his own arm's reach. It also segments the yellow truck retreating from the right foreground (~2–4 m in Frame 1) into the distance (~12 m in Frame 2), a parked white car angled on the right (~12–15 m away), the approaching motorcycle and rider on the right in Frame 4 (~4–5 m away, facing forward/left of the camera wearer), and the two people standing ~1 m apart near the right building stairs in Frames 1–3 (~7–9 m away, facing the street). On the left side, the map inconsistently labels the vendor cart (~1.5–2.5 m away, within arm's reach of the seated people behind it in Frames 4–5) as a massive 'truck' mask in Frames 1 and 3 and its top canopy as an 'umbrella' in Frames 2 and 4, while completely missing it in Frame 5. This map makes it easier than RGB alone to count and separate overlapping distant instances—such as distinguishing the scooter rider from the motorcycle in Frames 3–4 and separating the two standing bystanders on the right—despite heavy occlusion around the cart and parked vehicles. However, it is highly unreliable across time, misclassifying the vendor stall as a truck, failing to detect the black helmet within the camera wearer's arm's reach (<0.5 m in Frames 4–5), and dropping masks for the parked scooters on the left and the retreating yellow truck after Frame 2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black in Frames 1–3 and only detects a yellow body skeleton for the approaching pedestrian on the right in Frame 4 (~3–4 m away) and Frame 5 (~2 m away, just outside the camera wearer's arm's reach). In those final two frames, the skeleton's shoulder, hip, and head keypoints show his torso and face oriented toward the camera wearer while his legs are mid-stride and his left elbow is bent with his forearm raised, placing his hand within his own arm's reach in front of his chest. In Frame 5, his lower legs extend to the bottom edge of the frame where his left foot is partially cut off at the boundary. The pose map makes the pedestrian's limb articulation, stride phase, and forward-facing torso orientation in Frames 4–5 immediately explicit without visual clutter from his patterned shirt or the street background. However, the map is severely unreliable for broader scene understanding: it completely misses the pedestrian in Frames 1–3 (at 4–8 m), fails to render any magenta hand skeletons even at 2 m in Frame 5, and fails to detect all other people in the scene, including the scooter rider (~4–5 m in Frame 4), the bystanders on the right (~7–9 m), and the partially occluded people behind the left cart (~2.5–3.5 m).
